L9: # Title:Selection of Supervised Learning-based Sparse Matrix Reordering Algorithms
L10: 
L11: Authors:cite5†Tao Tang , cite6†Youfu Jiang , cite7†Yingbo Cui , cite8†Jianbin Fang , cite9†Peng Zhang , cite10†Lin Peng , cite11†Chun Huang L12:

L15: cite12†View PDF cite13†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:Sparse matrix ordering is a vital optimization technique often employed for solving large-scale sparse matrices. Its goal is to minimize the matrix bandwidth by reorganizing its rows and columns, thus enhancing efficiency.
L17: Conventional methods for algorithm selection usually depend on brute-force search or empirical knowledge, lacking the ability to adjust to diverse sparse matrix cite14†this http URL†structures.as a result, we have introduced a supervised learning-based model for choosing sparse matrix reordering algorithms.
L18: This model grasps the correlation between matrix characteristics and commonly utilized reordering algorithms, facilitating the automated and intelligent selection of the suitable sparse matrix reordering algorithm.
L19: Experiments conducted on the Florida sparse matrix dataset reveal that our model can accurately predict the optimal reordering algorithm for various matrices, leading to a 55.37% reduction in solution time compared to solely using the AMD reordering algorithm, with an average speedup ratio of 1.45.

L9: # Title:Optimizing CPU Cache Utilization in Cloud VMs with Accurate Cache Abstraction
L10: 
L11: Authors:cite6†Mani Tofigh , cite7†Edward Guo , cite8†Weiwei Jia , cite9†Xiaoning Ding , cite10†Jianchen Shan L12:

L15: cite11†View PDF cite12†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:This paper shows that cache-based optimizations are often ineffective in cloud virtual machines (VMs) due to limited visibility into and control over provisioned caches. In public clouds, CPU caches can be partitioned or shared among VMs, but a VM is unaware of cache provisioning details. Moreover, a VM cannot influence cache usage via page placement policies, as memory-to-cache mappings are hidden.
L17: The paper proposes a novel solution, CacheX, which probes accurate and fine-grained cache abstraction within VMs using eviction sets without requiring hardware or hypervisor support, and showcases the utility of the probed information with two new techniques: LLC contention-aware task scheduling and virtual color-aware page cache management.
L18: Our evaluation of CacheX's implementation in x86 Linux kernel demonstrates that it can effectively improve cache utilization for various workloads in public cloud VMs.

L10: 
L11: Authors:cite5†Michael Dang'ana , cite6†Yuqiu Zhang , cite7†Hans-Arno Jacobsen L12:

L15: cite8†View PDF cite9†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:Resource orchestration and configuration parameter search are key concerns for container-based infrastructure in cloud data centers. Large configuration search space and cloud uncertainties are often mitigated using contextual bandit techniques for resource orchestration including the state-of-the-art Drone orchestrator.
L17: Complexity in the cloud provider environment due to varying numbers of virtual machines introduces variability in workloads and resource metrics, making orchestration decisions less accurate due to increased nonlinearity and noise. Ksurf, a state-of-the-art variance-minimizing estimator method ideal for highly variable cloud data, enables optimal resource estimation under conditions of high cloud variability.
L18: > This work evaluates the performance of Ksurf on estimation-based resource orchestration tasks involving highly variable workloads when employed as a contextual multi-armed bandit objective function model for cloud scenarios using Drone.
L19: Ksurf enables significantly lower latency variance of $41\%$ at p95 and $47\%$ at p99, demonstrates a $4\%$ reduction in CPU usage and 7 MB reduction in master node memory usage on Kubernetes, resulting in a $7\%$ cost savings in average worker pod count on VarBench Kubernetes benchmark.
